reason: The current GraphRecommender reaches macro validation HR@10 of 0.6225, but encode_history scores individual events without contextualizing neighboring items; Electronics remains lowest at 0.435, which motivates testing local sequence context without establishing causality. Historical sequential-encoder successes support this hypothesis, while unsuccessful loss and embedding changes favor retaining the existing objective and tied graph representations. Modify model_design for the single residual causal convolution and training_evaluation for faithful reconstruction, targeted diagnostics, and validation.

In encode_history, mask gathered propagated item vectors before transposing to channels-first format, explicitly left-pad by two positions, apply the convolution and GELU, project back to dim, and add the original vectors through a residual connection. Mask the contextualized vectors again and use them as values and as inputs to the existing history_key calculation with unchanged relative-position embeddings, attention pooling, graph-user query, and fusion gate. This lets each history event represent itself and its two predecessors while preserving chronological order, repeated interactions, empty-history behavior, tied candidate embeddings, and the jointly learned item bias. Retain graph propagation, supervised-edge masking, model dimensions, loss, optimizer, and regularization; historical results motivate adding ordered context but do not justify replacing the backbone, untying embeddings, changing the objective, or adding a separate scorer.
